passages: Open in a new tab Broad variation in the findings from 73 teams testing the same hypothesis with the same data.
Even highly skilled scientists motivated to come to accurate results varied tremendously in what they found when provided with the same data and hypothesis to test.

This reveals a universe of uncertainty that remains hidden when considering a single study in isolation.

This six-question module is also the source of the data used by David Brady and Ryan Finnigan (19) in one of the most cited investigations of the substantive hypothesis participants were instructed to test.

This was followed by a request that the teams develop their own ideal models for testing the same hypothesis using potentially all of the provided data, but that they submit their analysis plan prior to running the models.
